# Using Maestro in Kiro

<!-- Generated by `node packages/cli build` from the harness registry. Do not edit by hand. -->

The skill is the same in every agent. This guide covers only what is specific to Kiro.

## Install

Project scope (one repository): copy this skill folder to `.kiro/skills/maestro/`.

User scope (every project): copy it to `~/.kiro/skills/maestro/`.

From the gti-skills repository, the CLI does the copy for you:

```bash
node packages/cli install --harness kiro --skill maestro
node packages/cli install --harness kiro --skill maestro --scope user
```

Restart the agent session after installing so it rescans its skills.

## Use

Describe the task in plain language. Kiro loads the skill when the request matches its `description`. You can also run it explicitly by typing `/maestro`.

## Where the skill finds its files

`<skill-dir>` in `SKILL.md` is the folder that contains `SKILL.md`: `.kiro/skills/maestro` for a project install, or `~/.kiro/skills/maestro` for a user install. Scripts and references are always addressed relative to it.

## Verify

Ask the agent which skills it has loaded and check that `maestro` is listed.

## Notes

- Workspace skills take priority over user skills with the same name.
- Maestro delegates every step. Load the model preferences and the provider catalog before choosing a worker. Paseo can drive Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Pi, Cline, Cursor, Kilo, Hermes, Antigravity, Muse, and ACP providers. Read references/harness/adapters.md before the first spawn, and record the worker chat id before the first prompt.
- Kiro has no standard resumable CLI session. Use a worker CLI from the adapter table when reviews must return to the same chat.
- Documentation: [Kiro](https://kiro.dev/docs/skills/) (path source: official).
